additions.reason: Da'at is the central concept of this entire Torah. It is the force that mediates between all opposites and makes shidduchim possible. The Torah opens: 'הַדַּעַת מְשַׁדֵּךְ כָּל הַשִּׁדּוּכִים' — Da'at makes all matches. Da'at is called a bechina of 'מִפִּיו דַּעַת וּתְבוּנָה' (from His mouth comes knowledge and understanding). It is the most dominant concept and needs a node in the dataset for this Torah.
additions.source_quote: הַדַּעַת הוּא הַמְתַוֵּךְ בֵּין שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים

additions.reason: Shidduch (match/union) is the core metaphor of this Torah. It is explicitly called a bechina of the union performed by da'at between two opposites. Torah itself is called a shidduch-maker (מְשַׁדֵּךְ שִׁדּוּכִין) when spoken by the tzaddik. The word שִׁידּוּךְ is an acronym for the verse about the priest's lips guarding da'at and Torah, tying the concept directly to the central nodes.
additions.source_quote: כְּשֶׁהַצַּדִּיק אוֹמֵר תּוֹרָה הוּא בְּחִינַת מְשַׁדֵּךְ שִׁדּוּכִין

additions.reason: The bar da'at (master of knowledge = the true tzaddik) is equated with the one who actualizes da'at. He is the human vessel through which da'at moves from potential to actuality, enabling the shidduch. He shares the same essential nature as da'at-in-action.
additions.source_quote: שֶׁצָּרִיךְ שֶׁיָּבוֹא לְהַבַּר־דַּעַת לִשְׁמֹעַ תּוֹרָה מִפִּיו

additions.reason: Da'at in potential is contrasted with da'at in actuality. It is a structural aspect (bechina) of da'at itself — the same force in its latent/unrealized state. It belongs to the same package as da'at and Torah/kallah because the entire Torah's argument turns on this distinction: when da'at is in potential it cannot perform the shidduch; it must exit to actuality via the tzaddik's mouth.
additions.source_quote: כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהַדַּעַת בְּכֹחַ, אֲזַי לִפְעָמִים אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְחַבֵּר הַמְשֻׁדָּכִים

notes: This Torah has an exceptionally sparse bechina dataset: only one bechina edge recorded. The Torah's conceptual density is much higher than the dataset reflects. Da'at is the central concept but has no node recorded. The single recorded bechina (תורה/כלה) is a genuine and important one but represents only one of several bechina-type statements in the text.
The eitza edge recorded (שיבוא להבר־דעת לשמע תורה מפיו → יכול למצא השדוך שלו) correctly captures the Torah's practical instruction as cause-and-effect, not bechina.

The Torah contains an interesting structural feature: שידוך (shidduch) itself contains שני הפכים (two opposites), Torah contains שני מיני אותיות (two types of letters), and the bechina Torah=כלה rests on both being unions of opposites — this is a second-order bechina worth noting.
